PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: prop-guardian-spear
Workflow profile: 2X3_VERTICAL (2:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Prop/artifact guard: transfer only material response, patina, highlight rolloff, and photographic presentation. Do not add a glowing sword, sacred symbols, blood, or human hands unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
GUARDIAN SPEAR — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: HERO PROP DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, SCALE, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Hero production-reference prop of Hell’s Guardian spear from the biblical epic JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL, shown as a complete freestanding weapon of supernatural fortress guards. This is the rank-and-file and leader-carried spear that drips a dark living substance before the Gate of Hell, and that turns to ash in the Guardian Leader’s hands when Jesus merely looks at him. Primary continuity state for this asset is the intact dark-dripping form; the ash-dissolve beat is a separate VFX continuity state that must share the same silhouette, length, and construction until disintegration begins.

Overall silhouette is a towering two-handed war spear sized for eight-foot armored Guardians: total length roughly nine to ten feet, shaft thick enough for gauntleted two-hand grip, head massive and cruel rather than refined. Proportions feel oversized for a human soldier yet physically coherent as forged war iron—brutal, ancient, ceremonial in its malice.

Shaft construction: a long column of blackened ironwood and corroded wrought iron banding fused along the grain. The wood is nearly charcoal-dark, with deep longitudinal splits, ash-grey mineral encrustation, and oily soot worked into every pore. Iron collars and helical wrap bands clamp the shaft at regular intervals; each band is pitted, blistered with rust bloom the color of dried blood and dead leaves, edges feathered by millennia of corrosion. Near the grip zone the shaft is wrapped in dark rawhide strips hardened like tar, crusted with old residue, worn smooth where gauntlets have held it for ages. A short iron butt-spike or ferrule finishes the base, squared and nicked, useful for planting in black stone.

Spearhead: a broad leaf-to-diamond blade of ancient black iron, leaf-shaped with a reinforced mid-rib, edges notched and chipped as if it has pierced armor and bone for centuries. The point is still lethal—needle-sharp under the grime—but the flats carry deep pitting, hammer scars, and a dull slate-to-obsidian patina rather than parade polish. Socket and langets run down the shaft in long iron tongues riveted through the wood; rivets are crude dome heads, some missing, some weeping dark residue. Along the lower socket, faint bone inlay or fused bone fragments appear locked into the metal—hell-forge craft that echoes the iron-and-bone Gate—subtle, not ornamental scrollwork.

The defining living property: a dark viscous substance drips slowly from the spearhead’s edges, point, and lower socket. It is thicker than blood, almost tar-black with a wet crimson under-sheen when cold blue torch light catches it, behaving as if alive—slow-crawling beads, elongated strands that stretch before dropping, a faint oily sheen and micro-bubbling as if the fluid itself resents stillness. Fresh drips gather at the tip and hang; older streaks trail down the mid-rib and stain the upper shaft in irregular rivulets that have dried to glossy black scabs. No bright modern chrome, no clean factory steel, no decorative fantasy runes or glowing sigils carved as readable symbols.

Material and texture language stays photoreal and tactile: subsurface grit in the rust, micro-flakes of scale lifting from the blade, matte soot versus wet tar-gloss of the living drip, hairline fractures in the ironwood, dust of black stone powder caught in crevices. Scale cues include the length relative to a neutral empty frame, the thickness of the grip, and the weight implied by heavy iron fittings.

Environment and lighting for the reference: isolated prop floating or resting against a minimal dark hell-fortress void—deep crimson and obsidian context, not a busy set. Key light is cold blue torch ambience approximately 2000K (#4169E1 range) raking across metal to read corrosion and wet drip edges; a low red underglow approximately 3500K warms the underside of the blade and pooled residue; subtle volumetric smoke haze carries motes of ash. No golden divine light on this prop in its intact guardian state. Color grade: deep crimsons, obsidian blacks, cold blue speculars, wet black-crimson drip highlights—pre-transformation hell palette.

Camera and framing: neutral production-reference hero framing with the complete spear fully visible tip-to-butt, slight three-quarter angle so blade face, mid-rib, dripping edge, socket, grip wrap, and butt-spike all read clearly; moderate depth of field keeping the entire weapon sharp enough for material matching; 2.39:1 cinematic widescreen feel without cropping the ends. Studio-clean isolation, not a handheld combat still.

Continuity locks: same spear geometry for rank Guardians raised before the Gate and for the Leader’s spear that becomes ash; always dark-dripping when intact; materials always corroded black iron, aged ironwood, rawhide grip, living dark viscous drip; no modern weapons, no firearms, no logos, no text, no watermarks, no labels, no UI. Sacred biblical-epic tone—supernatural dread of hell’s arsenal, not comic-book fantasy chrome. Neutral production reference framing, the complete object visible, accurate materials and scale, no labels or text.
